messages.author: fe832bdd27193376
messages.subject: change the "cross type"
parts:
Hi Karl,
my data were read as being f2.intercross. Is this the proper way how to
repair the issue? :

> class(HstQTL4)
[1] "f2" "cross"

> c("bc","cross")->class(HstQTL4)

> class(HstQTL4)
[1] "bc" "cross"

Regards, Radek

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: change the "cross type"
parts:
That's a correct way to change the cross type, but you should look more
carefully at the data and what led it to be called an intercross.
There's
likely something in the genotype data that is not correct, and so the
whole
thing could be garbled, even with the change in cross type.

If you send me the file, I could help you.

regards,
karl

messages.author: fe832bdd27193376
messages.subject: Re: change the "cross type"
parts:
I think, I have figured out the issue. The problem was that I had been
using symbols PP, PB, BB to mark the genotype combinations. The program
seems not to have liked this, since after I did the following change in
the csv data file before loading into workspace:

PB->AB ... (PWD/B6 allelic combination) on autosomes
BB->AA ... (B6/B6 allelic combination) on autosomes
PP->BB ... (B6/Y allelic combination) on X
BB->AA ... (PWD/Y allelic combination) on X

and added the "sex" column, the program loaded all data smoothly as a
backcross:

> HstQTL5 <- read.cross("csv", dir="/Users/Radek/Documents/Protocols/2006_05/0605HstQTL/",file="HstQTLbbedit5.csv",genotypes=c("AA","AB","BB", "not PP","not BB"),convertXdata=T)

--Read the following data:
53 individuals
119 markers
3 phenotypes
--Estimating genetic map

> summary(HstQTL5)
Backcross

No. individuals: 53

No. phenotypes: 3
Percent phenotyped: 100 100 100

No. chromosomes: 20
Total markers: 119
No. markers: 9 7 7 5 7 5 6 6 5 4 6 5 5 5 5 5 6 5 6 10
Percent genotyped: 100
Genotypes (%): AA:47 AB:53
>

I am sending out both data files in an email to you as well, named as
"oldVersion.csv" and "newVersion.csv".

Regards, Radek
